capture.final_message:
Use neighborhood characterizations throughout.

- For the first conjunct, regard \(X|_t : t \to \beta\). By construction, the topology on \(\beta\) is coinduced by this map, so \(X|_t\) is continuous. Pulling the neighborhood \(s\) of \(X(a)\) back gives a neighborhood of \(\langle a,h\rangle\) in the subtype \(t\). Translate subtype neighborhoods back to ambient neighborhoods within \(t\); this yields \(X^{-1}(s)\in\mathcal N[t](a)\).

- For the second conjunct, rewrite \(x\in\operatorname{interior}(s)\) as \(s\in\mathcal N(x)\). Since \(s\) and \(t\) are eventually equal in \(\mathcal N(x)\), filter membership is invariant under that eventual equality, so \(t\in\mathcal N(x)\). Converting back gives \(x\in\operatorname{interior}(t)\).

The useful intermediate goals are therefore the continuity of the coinducing map, the subtype-neighborhood/\(\mathrm{nhdsWithin}\) correspondence, and transfer of filter membership across `EventuallyEq`.
